questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Other

questions.question: Please explain: *
questions.answer: See down below.

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I wanted to go a place where there was amazing nature, and a high academic standard. These criteria was why I choose University of Calgary for my destination.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I had a great experience with the university and they were very helpful in the process of applying and arriving. Through my exhange they also helped a lot with figuring out the way of courses and so on. It was a great help, especially when you come as a new person to a foreign country.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: In general the university was very helpful and accommodating in the proces of arriving and so on. It was a bit difficult to figure information about courses, and in which semesters they are offered. But it was easy when we arrived, although it was a bit hard to figure out from home. The good thing was that the first two weeks are used to shop around and try out courses. For me that was a very nice way to do it, because i also found out that i didnt want some of the courses i applied for anyway.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: They had different orientation events for the new students. Among others, they had a tour around campus that new students could join.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to start in good time. I lived with 5 other exchange students in a airbnb around 30 min from campus by bus. It was a bit hard to find something that was affordable, but because we where so many people it made it a bit easier. I knew a lot of students who were also exchange students, who also lived off campus because there was a lot of pressure on housing on campus. Therefore, a lot of people had to find housing elsewhere. But overall my advice would be to start looking for it early and also write to other exhange students who need housing. It is a great way to meet people!

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I liked living off campus, but of course i would also have loved to try live on campus. It sounded like a lot of fun for the poeple who did so. For me at least, i lived pretty close to both downtown and campus, so living off campus was totally fine by me.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: They had too little housing on campus when i did my exchange. Off campus housing was difficult to find for a reasonable price, but it worked out in the end. But with that said, they were really helpful by providing information on where to look for housing. Additionally, UofC also provided a group chat for all exhange students, so that we could get in touch with each other. This was a great way for people to find housing off campus.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found it easy, it was pretty straight forward.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I applied for 5 different places, both in Canada and Europe. I found the registration proces pretty easy, and i would say that university of copenhagen provided the needed information to make the proces easier. When i applied, i afterwards got a letter from UofC, saying that i was accpeted and i had the choisce to decline or accept the spot for the fall semester.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I think the previous travel reports helped me to decide where i wanted to go. Furthermore, UofC also send different mails to help in the proces of registration in courses.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got all the classes i wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would recommend to register for more courses than you have to take. They have the first two weeks, where you are able to try out all the courses. And if you are registered for more than you need to have, you get the flexibility to choose which ones you want and still get the chance to try them out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The geography program was great. I really liked most of the courses i had.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The arctic system science was a undergraduate/graduate course. The level was good, and not too difficult but a really exciting course overall. The course i had at film studies was mostly for fun, but it turned out to be a really nice course.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The style of teaching at UofC is more like the danish high school, and in general very different than UCPH. It involves a lot of learning by remembering, because there is midterms and finals which often contains multiple choice/true false questions where your notes are not alllowed. Futhermore, some courses are graded on participations among other things, and it is therefore required to show up for lab and so on.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to film studies (FILM 201)
Government and politics of Africa (POLI 371)
Arctic system science (GEOG 502)
Wind science (GEOG 506)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would definitly recommend the arctic system science and wind science, they were great! both the instructors/professors where great at teaching and were very motivating in the learning proces.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I spend a lot of the money i had on hiking in the weekends in banff nationalpark. For me going out, was not a big part of the experience, but it was the nature and the mountains. I did not have unexpected cost in that sense, but i was surpriced how expensive shopping for food was.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Grocery shopping is in general more expensive than in copenhagen. Especially vegetables. My best advice is to go to either real canadian superstore or wallmarts! ;) Eating out is not as expensive as in copenhagen.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
In downtown Calgary, there is not much to do. There are some nice cafés/bars in kensington and inglewood, but there isnt much of clubs. There is a lot of ice hockey in the big stadion, which i would highly recommend to go and see. It is a lot of fun!
 Locals go to the mountains for recreational time, so if you like nature, hiking, skiing and so on i would highly recommend Calgary!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There is a lot of sport games at the university, that students can join for free. That is really fun to go and see!
I did not explore the cultural activities at UofC, but there is probably some. They had some social activities in start for new students, and i would highly recommend to join thoose. It is a good way to get to know people.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Icehockey, rodeo and the mountains. 
Rodeo was for sure a big experience, because it was so Alberta and very Canada. It was a lot of fun, because when i went we were a group of exchange students, and we were definetly the only ones who werent locals. It was a lot of fun to see and also a big cultural experince.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: If you are only in clagary for a short visit, my biggest recommendation is to go to  the mountains. It is stunning and overwhelming, bit so amazing to see!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think it was pretty easy. People are in general very welcoming and open. You can always ask locals and they will for sure help the best they can.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I found local canadian friends in my courses, that is probably the best tip i can give. Just talk with all the people, and you will meet some great people both exchange and locals.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I did not find the cultural differences challenging, i found the culture very welcoming and open minded.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Again, the welcoming and open culture.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Look for housing in good time, if you are gonna live off campus. 
Use the oppertunity for great nature close by. 
Enjoy the stay, and take the chances for experiences that you wouldnt get back home fx rodeo, hiking and so on!

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No, i dont think so

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The mix of great university experince and nature!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being in another country with a new culture. It is a great challenge, and also being so far from home and all the things you know. You learn a lot about how you work when trying to integrate into a new culture.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
